To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the COM can be accurately predicted by using a genetic algorithm sum of sinusoids model.

1) a genetic sum of sinesis model was developed that is able to accurately predict the trajectory of the center of mass in the frontal plane; 2) the sum of sinesis genetic model outperformed a neural network model and an adaptive fuzzy interface model; 3) the model was validated using data acquired from a multisegmental task on both fixed and foam surfaces; 4) the model was able to estimate the trajectory of the trunk segment COM with a mean absolute prediction error
the genetic algorithm sum of sine model is the most accurate model in estimating COM position.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of accelerometers to estimate the COM.
the development of a portable system to estimate the COM of the body during movement.
the development of a new technology for the assessment of the center of mass of the body during postural control.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the genetic sum of sine model was found to have the best overall performance.
a sum of sines genetic algorithm model was found to provide the most accurate estimate of COM, followed by the adaptive fuzzy interface model and the neural network.
the COM estimates are promising and the models can be applied for the assessment and training of patients with balance disorders.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a genetic sum of sinesis model can be used to predict the trajectory of the body's COM using only two acceleration signals.
we developed a system that can be used in clinical settings to assess balance and postural control, which is an important component of rehabilitation.
a hybrid genetic algorithm (GA) sum of sines (SOS) model can be used as an alternative method to predict the COM trajectory.

a portable system based on accelerometers is a promising tool for clinical applications.
the sum of sines approach is a promising method for the prediction of COM in a clinical environment.
